reflections.title: Resting Like a Weaned Child

reflect.text: When we try to carry burdens meant only for God, we quickly find ourselves filled with anxiety and despair. True humility means accepting our human limits and giving up self-reliance. Instead of chasing things too grand for us, we can intentionally learn to rest in God's presence.

David pictures this rest as a weaned child with its mother. At first, a nursing baby cries and struggles when weaning begins, not knowing this change helps it grow up. In our lives, daily interruptions and hardships are tools God uses to build Christlike character. As F. B. Meyer noted, God turns us away from early comforts so "the soul calms, becomes stilled and quieted." When we stop fighting and submit to His control, quiet peace forms in us.

A weaned child rests with its mother simply to enjoy her, not just to demand milk. In the same way, we can be content with God Himself rather than constantly begging for gifts. When we place our enduring hope in the Lord, our souls discover lasting rest.

questions: What burdens or daily interruptions have you been fighting against instead of trusting God?
How can you take time today simply to enjoy being in God's presence?
reflections.prayer: Lord, forgive us when pride makes us try to control things that belong to You. Please quiet our anxious hearts when life brings interruptions and uncomfortable changes. Teach us to rest gently in Your presence and to love You for who You are. Amen.

D3.author: Wyatt Graham
D3.work: Calm and Quiet in God’s Arms
